defect: Sentence 7 calls Seneca Village "a community of mostly African American homeowners." That overstates the record: about two-thirds of the roughly 225 residents (1855) were African American and about one-third were of Irish or German descent, and more than half of the African American households (not most residents) owned their land; many residents rented.
